records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy rare-earth perovskite nanofibers be synthesized via a glycothermal method and exhibit effective catalytic activity in low-temperature carbon monoxide oxidation?. System: (Y0.2La0.2Nd0.2Gd0.2Sm0.2)CoO3. Processing: Glycothermal method using 1,4-butanediol and diethylene glycol at 250 °C. Test conditions: CO oxidation at 25, 50, and 100 °C. Findings: 78% conversion of CO at 50 °C; 97% conversion of CO at 100 °C; High specific surface area of 27.3 m2 g−1; Uniform distribution of elements throughout the matrix; Significant reduction in energy consumption of approximately 52% compared to typical high-temperature synthesis methods. Mechanism: The incorporation of rare-earth elements into a high-entropy structure imparts unique catalytic properties, promoting a synergistic effect that enhances performance. Future work: Optimizing synthesis parameters to further enhance catalytic performance and exploring the mechanistic aspects of CO oxidation in high-entropy oxide catalysts. Quote: "the incorporation of rare-earth elements into a high-entropy structure could impart unique catalytic properties, promoting a synergistic effect that enhances performance"
